Search breadth: very thorough.

Repo: `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa`. READ-ONLY.

I need the PRECISE established pattern for building a Zimmermann design-system component, as it exists on the branch `feature/SFCC-55_global-footer-ui`. Do NOT check that branch out — read it with git (`git show <branch>:<path>`, `git ls-tree -r --name-only <branch> -- <path>`).

This is the reference implementation a new build must match exactly, so I need file-level specifics, not a summary.

## Read these in full and report their exact shape

Atoms (all five): `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/{zimmButton,zimmIcon,zimmLogo,zimmNavItem,zimmTextInput}/index.tsx` and each `index.stories.tsx`.
Molecule: `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmInputAction/index.tsx` and its story.
Recipes: `overrides/app/theme/components/{zimmNavItem,zimmTextInput,navConstants,index}.ts`, plus `recipeGuards.test.ts` and `zimmTextInput.test.ts`.
Also: `overrides/app/theme/fontFace.tsx`, and how it is mounted (grep for `ZimmFontFace` or `fontFace` across that branch).

## Report specifically

1. **File layout per component.** Exactly which files exist per atom. Which atoms have a recipe and which do not — and for the ones without, what they use instead. Which have a co-located test.
2. **Component file anatomy.** For each atom: the Props type (name, shape, where declared), the export style (named? default? both?), whether `forwardRef` is used, how styling is applied (`useStyleConfig`/`useMultiStyleConfig`/`chakra()` factory/direct props/`textStyle`), and whether JSDoc is present.
3. **Recipe anatomy.** For `zimmNavItem.ts` and `zimmTextInput.ts`: single-part or multipart, the `parts` array, `baseStyle`/`variants`/`sizes`/`defaultProps`, how values are expressed (bare token keys vs `var(--zimm-*)` vs raw literals) and on WHICH props each form is used. Note the exact naming convention for the registered theme key and how it is registered in `theme/components/index.ts`.
4. **`navConstants.ts`** — what it holds and why it is separate from a recipe.
5. **`recipeGuards.test.ts`** — what invariants it enforces, and whether it has a self-test proving it can fail.
6. **Story anatomy.** Title/category string, which named exports exist, when a `play` function is present, and what `storybook/test` imports are used.
7. **`zimmNavItem`'s full API** — every prop, its type, defaults, and what it renders in each branch (anchor vs button). I specifically need to know whether it could serve as a breadcrumb crumb link, and what a `breadcrumb` variant would need to add.
8. **Anything that looks like a deliberate deviation from the repo's written rules**, with the file and line, so I don't mistake it for a mistake to copy.

## Output
Report directly in your final message — no file writing needed. Be concrete: quote the actual code shapes (short excerpts), give `path:line` references, and clearly separate what you VERIFIED by reading from anything you inferred.

     1	import { defineStyleConfig } from '@chakra-ui/react';
     2	
     3	// Vertical leading around the label. Figma's footer-item allows equal space above and
     4	// below the text and lets the item height follow the line count — 24px for one line,
     5	// 38px for two (node 40000407:11736 > About Section > Links). Its text boxes are
     6	// cap-height (8px one line, 22px two) where a browser line box is not, so the rule
     7	// transfers rather than the numbers. The inner span reserves 1px for the underline
     8	// indicator, so a line box measures 15px and two measure 29px; 4.5px each side yields
     9	// 15+9=24 and 29+9=38 exactly. No 4.5px entry exists in spacing.ts — same provisional
    10	// treatment as button.ts's BTN_PADDING_Y, pending UI-designer sign-off.
    11	const NAV_ITEM_PAD_Y = '4.5px';
    12	
    13	const baseStyle = {
    14	  // textStyle is expanded in place by Chakra's style engine; fontFamily below
    15	  // deliberately overrides it — Figma Default/Navigation binds brand/font/family/body,
    16	  // not the heading family textStyles.navigation carries.
    17	  textStyle: 'navigation',
    18	  fontFamily: 'var(--zimm-font-family-body)',
    19	  display: 'inline-flex',
    20	  // Figma h-[24px] is a FLOOR, not a fixed height — the design's own ABOUT column
    21	  // wraps "ACKNOWLEDGEMENT OF COUNTRY" onto two lines. minHeight keeps the 24px
    22	  // target while letting multi-line labels grow, so no caller needs to override it.
    23	  minHeight: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)', // 1.5rem (24px) — Figma: h-[24px]
    24	  // Height comes from lineHeight + padding, not from centring inside minHeight.
    25	  // Centring only distributes space a single line leaves over, so a wrapped label
    26	  // overflowed the floor and lost its leading entirely — the second line of
    27	  // "ACKNOWLEDGEMENT OF COUNTRY" sat flush against the item above it.
    28	  lineHeight: 'var(--zimm-font-lineheight-4xs)', // 0.875rem (14px)
    29	  paddingBlock: NAV_ITEM_PAD_Y,
    30	  justifyContent: 'center',
    31	  alignItems: 'center',
    32	  whiteSpace: 'normal',
    33	  cursor: 'pointer',
    34	  background: 'none',
    35	  border: 'none',
    36	  // paddingInline, not the `padding` shorthand: a shorthand here would sit after
    37	  // paddingBlock above and reset it back to 0.
    38	  paddingInline: 0,
    39	  textDecoration: 'none',
    40	  // Inner span carries the underline. Use transparent instead of 'none' so
    41	  // border-color transitions smoothly on hover/active without a display change.
    42	  '& > span': {
    43	    borderBottom: 'var(--zimm-border-width-default) solid transparent',
    44	    transition: `border-color var(--zimm-motion-duration-fast) var(--zimm-motion-easing-standard)`,
    45	  },
    46	  _hover: {
    47	    '& > span': { borderBottomColor: 'currentColor' },
    48	  },
    49	  // Active (aria-current="page"): permanent underline regardless of hover
    50	  '&[aria-current="page"] > span': {
    51	    borderBottomColor: 'currentColor',
    52	  },
    53	};
    54	
    55	const variants = {
    56	  light: {
    57	    color: 'var(--zimm-color-text-default)',
    58	    _focusVisible: {
    59	      outline: 'var(--zimm-focus-ring)',
    60	      outlineOffset: 'var(--zimm-focus-ring-offset-default)',
    61	      boxShadow: 'none',
    62	    },
    63	  },
    64	  inverse: {
    65	    color: 'var(--zimm-color-text-inverse)',
    66	    _focusVisible: {
    67	      outline: 'var(--zimm-border-width-default) solid var(--zimm-color-text-inverse)',
    68	      outlineOffset: 'var(--zimm-focus-ring-offset-default)',
    69	      boxShadow: 'none',
    70	    },
    71	  },
    72	};
    73	
    74	export const ZimmNavItem = defineStyleConfig({
    75	  baseStyle,
    76	  variants,
    77	  defaultProps: { variant: 'light' },
    78	});

=========== theme/components/zimmTextInput.ts ===========
     1	import type { SystemStyleObject } from '@chakra-ui/react';
     2	
     3	// Figma Textfield flush variant (node 40000265:374): field/border/* tokens.
     4	// hover and filled (has value, unfocused) both darken to focus colour per Figma spec.
     5	const BORDER = {
     6	  default: 'var(--zimm-color-border-forms)', // #707070 — Figma field/border/default
     7	  hover: 'var(--zimm-color-border-focus)', // #191919 — Figma field/border/hover
     8	  filled: 'var(--zimm-color-border-focus)', // #191919 — Figma field/border/filled
     9	  focus: 'var(--zimm-color-border-focus)', // #191919 — Figma field/border/focus
    10	  error: 'var(--zimm-color-status-error)', // #9c0000 — Figma field/border/error
    11	} as const;
    12	
    13	// Figma field/border/inverse/default = white (opaque), inverse/error = #f98f8c (coral).
    14	// Figma does not spec inverse/hover or inverse/focus separately — same white as default.
    15	const BORDER_INVERSE = {
    16	  default: 'var(--zimm-color-text-inverse)',
    17	  hover: 'var(--zimm-color-text-inverse)',
    18	  filled: 'var(--zimm-color-text-inverse)',
    19	  focus: 'var(--zimm-color-text-inverse)',
    20	  error: 'var(--zimm-color-status-error-bg)', // #f98f8c
    21	} as const;
    22	
    23	// Figma: Textfield flush floated label — brand/font/size/250 (10px) / medium weight.
    24	const LABEL_FLOATED_SIZE = 'var(--zimm-font-size-4xs)';
    25	const LABEL_FLOATED_WEIGHT = 'var(--zimm-font-weight-medium)';
    26	// Figma: content div h-[36px] — pending alias/size/field/height token from the designer.
    27	// rem, not px: this height participates in a rem-derived measurement, so it has to scale with the
    28	// root font-size (WCAG 1.4.4 — see overrideStyling.md > Units). footer.ts's SIZE_SUBSCRIBE_SLOT
    29	// (2.8125rem) documents itself as "36px content + 4px/4px padding + 1px border"; freezing the
    30	// content height in px broke that derivation as soon as the root font-size moved — at 200% zoom the
    31	// slot reached 90px while the field reached only 53px, over-reserving by ~37px. (Dead space, not
    32	// clipping — the no-layout-shift guarantee held either way.) In rem it holds at every zoom level.
    33	// theme/components/ is Tier 2 (owner: UI designer) and SIZE_SUBSCRIBE_SLOT is already annotated
    34	// PROVISIONAL pending Kiera — this should ride along with that sign-off, not land silently.
    35	const FIELD_CONTENT_HEIGHT = '2.25rem'; // 36px at the default 16px root
    36	// No opacity token in foundation yet — pending Tier 1 PR with UI-designer sign-off.
    37	const OPACITY_DISABLED = 0.4;
    38	
    39	const MOTION = 'var(--zimm-motion-duration-fast) var(--zimm-motion-easing-standard)';
    40	
    41	/** State the component feeds in so the recipe can resolve the Figma colour cascade. */
    42	export type ZimmTextInputStyleProps = {
    43	  inverse?: boolean;
    44	  disabled?: boolean;
    45	  hasError?: boolean;
    46	  focused?: boolean;
    47	  /** Field has a value. Combined with `focused` this gives the floated-label state. */
    48	  filled?: boolean;
    49	};
    50	
    51	const palette = (inverse?: boolean) => (inverse ? BORDER_INVERSE : BORDER);
    52	
    53	/** Border colour precedence: disabled > error > focus > filled > default. */
    54	export const resolveBorderColour = ({ inverse, disabled, hasError, focused, filled }: ZimmTextInputStyleProps) => {
    55	  const p = palette(inverse);
    56	  if (disabled) return p.default;
    57	  if (hasError) return p.error;
    58	  if (focused) return p.focus;
    59	  if (filled) return p.filled;
    60	  return p.default;
    61	};
    62	
    63	/** In error the hover colour holds (error > hover); otherwise it darkens to focus. */
    64	export const resolveHoverBorderColour = (props: ZimmTextInputStyleProps) =>
    65	  props.hasError ? resolveBorderColour(props) : palette(props.inverse).hover;
    66	
    67	// Figma text/subtle = #666 for the floated/disabled label in light mode;
    68	// text/inverse/subtle = #969696 in inverse mode.
    69	export const resolveLabelColour = ({ inverse, disabled, focused, filled }: ZimmTextInputStyleProps) => {
    70	  const floated = Boolean(focused || filled);
    71	  if (disabled) return inverse ? 'var(--zimm-color-text-inverse-grey)' : 'var(--zimm-color-text-secondary)';
    72	  if (inverse) return floated ? 'var(--zimm-color-text-inverse-grey)' : 'var(--zimm-color-text-inverse)';
    73	  return floated ? 'var(--zimm-color-text-secondary)' : 'var(--zimm-color-text-default)';
    74	};
    75	
    76	export const ZimmTextInput = {
    77	  parts: ['root', 'row', 'content', 'label', 'input', 'clearButton', 'helper', 'error'],
    78	  baseStyle: (props: ZimmTextInputStyleProps): Record<string, SystemStyleObject> => {
    79	    const { inverse, disabled, focused, filled } = props;
    80	    const floated = Boolean(focused || filled);
    81	    const textColour = inverse ? 'var(--zimm-color-text-inverse)' : 'var(--zimm-color-text-default)';
    82	
    83	    return {
    84	      root: {
    85	        display: 'block',
    86	        width: '100%',
    87	        opacity: disabled ? OPACITY_DISABLED : 1,
    88	      },
    89	
    90	      // Flush bottom-border row. Hover is a CSS pseudo-class, not JS state.
    91	      row: {
    92	        display: 'flex',
    93	        alignItems: 'center',
    94	        gap: 'xs',
    95	        borderBottom: `var(--zimm-border-width-default) solid ${resolveBorderColour(props)}`,
    96	        paddingTop: '2xs',
    97	        paddingBottom: '2xs',
    98	        // not in Figma — UX animation on border-colour state changes
    99	        transition: `border-color ${MOTION}`,
   100	        _hover: disabled ? undefined : { borderBottomColor: resolveHoverBorderColour(props) },
   101	      },
   102	
   103	      // Figma: content flex-[1_0_0] h-[36px]
   104	      content: { flex: 1, position: 'relative', minHeight: FIELD_CONTENT_HEIGHT },
   105	
   106	      label: {
   107	        position: 'absolute',
   108	        left: 0,
   109	        fontFamily: 'var(--zimm-font-family-body)',
   110	        fontWeight: floated ? LABEL_FLOATED_WEIGHT : 'var(--zimm-font-weight-regular)',
   111	        fontSize: floated ? LABEL_FLOATED_SIZE : 'var(--zimm-font-size-2xs)',
   112	        lineHeight: floated ? undefined : 'var(--zimm-font-lineheight-2xs)',
   113	        color: resolveLabelColour(props),
   114	        top: floated ? '3xs' : '50%',
   115	        transform: floated ? 'none' : 'translateY(-50%)',
   116	        transition: `top ${MOTION}, transform ${MOTION}, font-size ${MOTION}, color ${MOTION}`,
   117	        whiteSpace: 'nowrap',
   118	      },
   119	
   120	      input: {
   121	        position: 'absolute',
   122	        bottom: 0,
   123	        left: 0,
   124	        right: 0,
   125	        width: '100%',
   126	        height: 'var(--zimm-scale-l)', // 20px — var, not 'l': theme.sizes has no 'l' key
   127	        background: 'transparent',
   128	        border: 'none',
   129	        outline: 'none',
   130	        fontFamily: 'var(--zimm-font-family-body)',
   131	        fontWeight: 'var(--zimm-font-weight-regular)',
   132	        fontSize: 'var(--zimm-font-size-2xs)',
   133	        color: textColour,
   134	        padding: 0,
   135	        opacity: floated ? 1 : 0,
   136	        cursor: disabled ? 'not-allowed' : 'text',
   137	        transition: `opacity ${MOTION}`,
   138	      },
   139	
   140	      clearButton: {
   141	        background: 'transparent',
   142	        border: 'none',
   143	        padding: 0,
   144	        cursor: 'pointer',
   145	        display: 'inline-flex',
   146	        alignItems: 'center',
   147	        justifyContent: 'center',
   148	        flexShrink: 0,
   149	        color: textColour,
   150	        // WCAG 2.2 AA SC 2.5.8 — 24px minimum target size
   151	        // var, not 'xl': min-width/height resolve via theme.sizes (xl = 36rem), not theme.space
   152	        minWidth: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)',
   153	        minHeight: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)',
   154	        // WCAG 2.2 AA SC 2.4.7 — visible focus state
   155	        _focusVisible: {
   156	          outline: inverse
   157	            ? 'var(--zimm-border-width-default) solid var(--zimm-color-text-inverse)'
   158	            : 'var(--zimm-focus-ring)',
   159	          outlineOffset: 'var(--zimm-focus-ring-offset-default)',
   160	          boxShadow: 'none',

     5	 * `components/` (per-component overrides). Add a new component override by

    14	 */

    16	import { extendTheme, type ThemeOverride } from '@chakra-ui/react';
    17	import { borderWidths, breakpoints, colors, fonts, spacing, textStyles } from './foundation';

    19	import { globalStyles } from './globalStyles';

    22	// <Global> in _app-config/index.tsx (ZimmTokensGlobal). They cannot go through
    23	// Chakra's styles.global because Chakra's style processor strips quotes from
    24	// font-family values like "'Futura Round', sans-serif", outputting just "sans-serif".
    25	//

    27	// Which foundations are registered as Chakra scales, and which are not
    28	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    29	// Registered below: borderWidths, breakpoints, colors, fonts, space, textStyles.
    30	//
    31	// Deliberately NOT registered, because the Zimmermann scale and the Chakra scale
    32	// use the same key names for different values — remapping them would silently
    33	// restyle the base retail-react-app, which uses those names at ~199 call sites:
    34	//
    35	//   fontSizes    Chakra md=16px xs=12px 2xs=10px 3xs=7.2px
    36	//                Zimmermann md=24px xs=16px 2xs=14px 3xs=12px  (4 collisions)
    37	//   transition   Chakra duration.fast=150ms slow=300ms
    38	//                Zimmermann fast=200ms default=300ms slow=500ms
    39	//   sizes        Chakra sizes.lg=32rem vs iconSizes.lg=20px
    40	//
    41	// Set type with `textStyle` (all 22 Handover text styles are registered), never a
    42	// raw `fontSize` token. For motion, icon and action dimensions, import the
    43	// constants from `foundation/` directly — the pattern component overrides already
    44	// use for FONT_MEDIUM. `theme/index.test.tsx` guards these scales against being
    45	// remapped by a future change.
    46	//
    47	// The 15 numeric `--zimm-scale-NNN` aliases are duplicates of the named scale
    48	// (400 = 16px = `m`) and exist only for the .zimm-* global classes; the named
    49	// scale is the Chakra-facing surface.
    50	
    51	const overrides: ThemeOverride = {

    53	  breakpoints,
    54	  colors,
    55	  fonts,
    56	  space: spacing,
    57	  textStyles,
    58	  components,
    59	  styles: {
    60	    global: globalStyles,
    61	  },
    62	};
    63	
    64	const theme = extendTheme(baseTheme, overrides);
    65	
    66	export default theme;

content.content: === .claude/rules/components.md === 1 # Components, Hooks & Storybook 2 3 Everything about designing, structuring, and presenting a React component or hook in this 4 project. Split out of [conventions.md](./conventions.md) — see that file for cross-cutting 5 rules that apply to every file regardless of type (TypeScript-only, DRY/KISS/SOLID, magic 6 numbers, security). TypeScript idioms live in [typescript.md](./typescript.md); Chakra/CSS 7 conventions live in [css.md](./css.md). 8 9 --- 10 11 ## Components 12 13 - **Named export** matches the folder name (e.g. `productTile/` exports `ProductTile`). 14 No default exports of anonymous functions. 15 - **Props type name** matches the component name: `ProductTileProps` for `ProductTile`, 16 `TopNavProps` for `TopNav`. 17 - **Props type placement:** 18 - _Default:_ declare the `Props` type at the top of the component file. 19 - _Move to `types.ts` in the same folder_ only when (a) the type is consumed by sibling 20 files (story, test, sub-components) **or** (b) it exceeds ~30 lines and mixes with 21 other shared types worth co-locating. 22 - The trigger is _shared consumption_, not line count alone. 23 - **JSDoc** is required on: 24 25 - Any component used by ≥2 callers (shared components — typically Tier 2 in 26 [protectedFiles.md](./protectedFiles.md)). 27 - Any exported hook. 28 - Any utility function with non-obvious behaviour. 29 30 Leaf components used by a single page don't need JSDoc — the prop type is sufficient. 31 32 - **Callback props** follow `onEventName` (e.g. `onAddToCart`, `onClose`). 33 - **Required props are non-optional;** optional props use `?` — no `| undefined` unions 34 for "I forgot to mark it optional." 35 - **Accessibility (JSX) — mechanically enforced by `.coderabbit/ast-grep-rules/`, so get 36 these right at authoring time:** 37 - Every `` needs an `alt` attribute (`alt=""` is fine for purely decorative images). 38 - Every `IconButton` (including wrapped variants like `IconButtonWithRegistration`) needs 39 an `aria-label` — it renders no visible text, so screen readers have nothing else to 40 announce. 41 - Any element with an `onClick` that isn't natively interactive (`div`, `span`, `Box`, 42 `Flex`, `Stack`, `VStack`, `HStack`, `Grid`, `Text`, and similar) needs a `role` 43 attribute at minimum — and for real keyboard operability, also `tabIndex={0}` and an 44 `onKeyDown` handler (or just use a `Button`/native interactive element instead, which 45 is almost always simpler than reimplementing keyboard behaviour). 46 47 --- 48 49 ## Composition — writing a "clean" component 50 51 Rules of thumb for when a component is doing too much and should be split, or when inline 52 state belongs in a custom hook instead. 53 54 - **Complexity / size.** A component function should stay roughly under ~150 lines and 55 avoid deep branching (rule of thumb: ~10-15 cyclomatic complexity — count independent 56 paths through the render logic, not total lines). **This is not currently ESLint-enforced** 57 — `.eslintrc.js` has no `max-lines-per-function` or `complexity` rule configured today, so 58 treat this as a self-check during authoring and something `/code-quality` should flag, not 59 something the build will fail on yet. If this keeps being a problem in practice, adding 60 those two ESLint rules is a cheap follow-up (they're built into ESLint core, no new 61 dependency needed). 62 - **Container/presentational separation.** Anything under `overrides/app/components/` 63 receives data as props — it does not call data-fetching hooks itself (SDK hooks like 64 `useCurrentBasket`/`useCurrentCustomer`/`useProduct`, or any `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` 65 / React Query hook). Data-fetching belongs in `overrides/app/pages/` or another container 66 component, which then passes the result down. This generalizes the existing 67 "no commerce state hooks inside leaf components" rule to _all_ data-fetching, not just 68 commerce SDK hooks — the reasoning is the same either way: a component that owns its own 69 data-fetching can't be reused somewhere the data arrives differently (SSR-prefetched, 70 mocked in Storybook, composed from a parent that already has it). 71 - **Extract-to-hook threshold.** Pull inline component logic out into a custom hook 72 (`overrides/app/hooks/use.ts`) when either is true: 73 74 - The component has ≥2 pieces of related `useState` that change together (a strong signal 75 the state belongs in one place, whether that's a custom hook or a single reducer). 76 - Any `useEffect` has a non-trivial dependency array or a cleanup function — non-trivial 77 meaning more than a single obvious dependency, or the effect does anything beyond a 78 one-line side effect. 79 80 This one is judgment-heavy, not a hard mechanical gate — `/code-quality` should flag it as 81 a should-fix, not a must-fix, and a component with ≥4 `useState` calls is a reasonable 82 coarse trigger to at least stop and ask "should this be a hook?" 83 84 --- 85 86 ## Hooks 87 88 - **File extension** is `.ts` (no JSX in a hook file). 89 - **Exported function name** matches the filename: `useWishlist.ts` exports `useWishlist`. 90 - **Parameters and return value are typed** — no implicit `any`, no missing return type. 91 See [typescript.md](./typescript.md) for the general typing rules this extends. 92 - **JSDoc** is required on every exported hook, including a `@returns` description. 93 94 --- 95 96 ## Storybook 97 98 Storybook is the canonical place to view components in isolation. Keep it browsable — 99 a flat 200-story sidebar is unusable. 100 101 ### When a story is required 102 103 - **Required** for any component exported from its folder under `overrides/app/components/` 104 or `overrides/app/pages/` (i.e. anything another file imports). 105 - **Not required** for purely internal sub-components that only render inside one parent 106 (e.g. `productTile/priceRow.tsx` used only by `productTile/index.tsx`). Cover their 107 variants via the parent's stories. 108 - Pages get a story showing the full assembly with representative props — not a story per 109 sub-section. 110 111 ### Categorisation 112 113 Story `title` drives the sidebar tree. Pick the first matching category: 114 115 | Category | What goes here | 116 | ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | 117 | `Foundation/` | Design tokens — Colour, Typography, Spacing, Icons, Shadows | 118 | `Elements/` | Generic building blocks — both display (Badge, Tag, Link, Avatar, Skeleton) and interactive controls (Button, Input, Checkbox, Select). Tiebreaker: _can it be used outside a form?_ → `Elements/`. | 119 | `Layout/` | Global chrome, navigation, and structural components — Header, Footer, DrawerMenu, ListMenu, Breadcrumb, Pagination, Seo | 120 | `Commerce/` | Commerce-specific shared components — ProductTile, OrderSummary, PromoCode, DisplayPrice, SwatchGroup | 121 | `Forms/` | Composed form assemblies — AddressForm, CheckoutContactForm, NewsletterSignup | 122 | `Pages/` | Full page assemblies — PDP, PLP, Cart, Checkout, Account | 123 | `Contentful/` | CMS-driven components — HeroBanner, RichText, ContentBlock. Use mock Contentful data in stories so variants are visible without a live CMS connection. | 124 125 Naming convention: singular for a concept or proper noun (`Foundation`, `Commerce`, `Layout`, `Contentful`); plural for a collection (`Elements`, `Forms`, `Pages`). 126 127 Examples: 128 129 ```ts 130 export default { title: 'Commerce/ProductTile' }; // ✅ 131 export default { title: 'Layout/Header' }; // ✅ 132 export default { title: 'Elements/Button' }; // ✅ 133 export default { title: 'Pages/PDP' }; // ✅ 134 export default { title: 'Elements/DisplayPrice' }; // ❌ — eCommerce specific, use Commerce/ 135 export default { title: 'Primitives/Button' }; // ❌ — use Elements/ 136 ``` 137 138 When in doubt: ask "what does this component _know_ about?" Commerce → `Commerce/`, 139 CMS-driven → `Contentful/`, nothing domain-specific → `Elements/`, page-level composition → `Pages/`. 140 141 ### Story content 142 143 - Every story file has a `Default` named export. 144 - Add named exports for meaningful states (`Loading`, `OutOfStock`, `WithDiscount`) — not 145 for every possible prop combination. 146 - `play` functions only when there's interactive behaviour worth asserting; otherwise the 147 story is purely visual.

This generalizes the existing 67 "no commerce state hooks inside leaf components" rule to _all_ data-fetching, not just 68 commerce SDK hooks — the reasoning is the same either way: a component that owns its own 69 data-fetching can't be reused somewhere the data arrives differently (SSR-prefetched, 70 mocked in Storybook, composed from a parent that already has it). 71 - **Extract-to-hook threshold.** Pull inline component logic out into a custom hook 72 (`overrides/app/hooks/use.ts`) when either is true: 73 74 - The component has ≥2 pieces of related `useState` that change together (a strong signal 75 the state belongs in one place, whether that's a custom hook or a single reducer). 76 - Any `useEffect` has a non-trivial dependency array or a cleanup function — non-trivial 77 meaning more than a single obvious dependency, or the effect does anything beyond a 78 one-line side effect. 79 80 This one is judgment-heavy, not a hard mechanical gate — `/code-quality` should flag it as 81 a should-fix, not a must-fix, and a component with ≥4 `useState` calls is a reasonable 82 coarse trigger to at least stop and ask "should this be a hook?" 83 84 --- 85 86 ## Hooks 87 88 - **File extension** is `.ts` (no JSX in a hook file). 89 - **Exported function name** matches the filename: `useWishlist.ts` exports `useWishlist`. 90 - **Parameters and return value are typed** — no implicit `any`, no missing return type. 91 See [typescript.md](./typescript.md) for the general typing rules this extends. 92 - **JSDoc** is required on every exported hook, including a `@returns` description. 93 94 --- 95 96 ## Storybook 97 98 Storybook is the canonical place to view components in isolation. Keep it browsable — 99 a flat 200-story sidebar is unusable. 100 101 ### When a story is required 102 103 - **Required** for any component exported from its folder under `overrides/app/components/` 104 or `overrides/app/pages/` (i.e. anything another file imports). 105 - **Not required** for purely internal sub-components that only render inside one parent 106 (e.g. `productTile/priceRow.tsx` used only by `productTile/index.tsx`). Cover their 107 variants via the parent's stories. 108 - Pages get a story showing the full assembly with representative props — not a story per 109 sub-section. 110 111 ### Categorisation 112 113 Story `title` drives the sidebar tree. Pick the first matching category: 114 115 | Category | What goes here | 116 | ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | 117 | `Foundation/` | Design tokens — Colour, Typography, Spacing, Icons, Shadows | 118 | `Elements/` | Generic building blocks — both display (Badge, Tag, Link, Avatar, Skeleton) and interactive controls (Button, Input, Checkbox, Select). Tiebreaker: _can it be used outside a form?_ → `Elements/`. | 119 | `Layout/` | Global chrome, navigation, and structural components — Header, Footer, DrawerMenu, ListMenu, Breadcrumb, Pagination, Seo | 120 | `Commerce/` | Commerce-specific shared components — ProductTile, OrderSummary, PromoCode, DisplayPrice, SwatchGroup | 121 | `Forms/` | Composed form assemblies — AddressForm, CheckoutContactForm, NewsletterSignup | 122 | `Pages/` | Full page assemblies — PDP, PLP, Cart, Checkout, Account | 123 | `Contentful/` | CMS-driven components — HeroBanner, RichText, ContentBlock. Use mock Contentful data in stories so variants are visible without a live CMS connection. | 124 125 Naming convention: singular for a concept or proper noun (`Foundation`, `Commerce`, `Layout`, `Contentful`); plural for a collection (`Elements`, `Forms`, `Pages`). 126 127 Examples: 128 129 ```ts 130 export default { title: 'Commerce/ProductTile' }; // ✅ 131 export default { title: 'Layout/Header' }; // ✅ 132 export default { title: 'Elements/Button' }; // ✅ 133 export default { title: 'Pages/PDP' }; // ✅ 134 export default { title: 'Elements/DisplayPrice' }; // ❌ — eCommerce specific, use Commerce/ 135 export default { title: 'Primitives/Button' }; // ❌ — use Elements/ 136 ``` 137 138 When in doubt: ask "what does this component _know_ about?" Commerce → `Commerce/`, 139 CMS-driven → `Contentful/`, nothing domain-specific → `Elements/`, page-level composition → `Pages/`. 140 141 ### Story content 142 143 - Every story file has a `Default` named export. 144 - Add named exports for meaningful states (`Loading`, `OutOfStock`, `WithDiscount`) — not 145 for every possible prop combination. 146 - `play` functions only when there's interactive behaviour worth asserting; otherwise the 147 story is purely visual.

    23	- Storybook story is mandatory; Vitest only when the component owns non-trivial logic.

    28

    30	   - Functional React component, named export (`export function <ComponentName>`) plus default export.
    31	   - `type <ComponentName>Props = { ... }` at the top of the file.
    32	   - JSDoc above the component if it will be consumed by ≥2 callers (shared/Tier 2).
    33	   - Chakra primitives for layout (`Box`, `Flex`, `Text`, etc.) using theme tokens — no hardcoded hex, pixel spacing, or raw font sizes.
    34	   - No data-fetching hooks of any kind (commerce SDK hooks like `useCurrentBasket`/`useCurrentCustomer`/`useProduct`, or React Query) — accept data as props; the parent (a page or container component) owns data fetching. See components.md → Composition → Container/presentational separation.
    35

=== conventions.md ===
     1	# Code Conventions
     2	
     3	Cross-cutting code-writing rules that apply to every file in a PR, regardless of type. Domain-specific
     4	conventions are split into their own files — see **See also** below. Both
     5	[.claude/skills/new-component/](../skills/new-component/SKILL.md) (when scaffolding) and
     6	[.claude/skills/code-quality/](../skills/code-quality/SKILL.md) (when auditing) reference this
     7	file and its siblings. Update the relevant file once — both skills, and (via
     8	[scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs](../../scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs)) all other AI tool configs,
     9	pick it up.
    10	
    11	> Higher-level project rules live in [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md). Tier classifications live in
    12	> [frozenFiles.md](./frozenFiles.md) and [protectedFiles.md](./protectedFiles.md).
    13	
    14	## See also
    15	
    16	- **[typescript.md](./typescript.md)** — TypeScript idioms: `any`/`type` vs `interface`,
    17	  discriminated unions, utility types, `satisfies`, `readonly`, generics.
    18	- **[css.md](./css.md)** — Chakra token usage, hardcoded-value policy, `.scss` conventions.
    19	- **[components.md](./components.md)** — component/hook/Storybook structure and the
    20	  composition rules for a "clean" component (complexity limits, container/presentational
    21	  separation, extract-to-hook threshold).
    22	- **[testing.md](./testing.md)** — Vitest / Storybook `play` / Playwright layer selection.
    23	- **[frozenFiles.md](./frozenFiles.md)** / **[protectedFiles.md](./protectedFiles.md)** —
    24	  Tier 1 / Tier 2 file protection.
    25	
    26	---
    27	
    28	## General — every file in a PR
    29	
    30	These apply to all `.ts`/`.tsx` files Claude creates or modifies, regardless of folder.
    31	
    32	- **TypeScript only inside `overrides/`.** `.js`/`.jsx` is not acceptable here — see AGENTS.md.
    33	- **No commented-out code blocks introduced by this PR** unless accompanied by an explicit
    34	  strong reason in a comment immediately above. Existing comments are preserved per AGENTS.md —
    35	  the rule is about _introducing_ new dead code, not removing old.
    36	- **No `console.log` or `console.error` calls** outside of error boundaries or explicit
    37	  developer-tooling files. Use the project's logger when one is introduced.
    38	- **No hardcoded design values** — Chakra token usage is a whole topic of its own now; see
    39	  [css.md](./css.md).
    40	- **React rules of hooks apply everywhere hooks are called.** Only call hooks at the top
    41	  level of a component or another hook. No conditional, looped, or nested hook calls.
    42	- **TypeScript idioms** (`any`, `type` vs `interface`, and the rest) — see
    43	  [typescript.md](./typescript.md).
    44	- **Australian spelling** in Zimmermann-authored identifiers and copy (`colour`, `centre`,
    45	  `organisation`). Override files keep upstream Salesforce spelling verbatim.
    46	- **Apply DRY, KISS, and SOLID.** Don't repeat logic — extract to a shared utility or hook
    47	  once the same pattern appears in two places. Prefer the simplest design that works; resist
    48	  speculative abstractions. Keep modules to a single responsibility; split a file when it
    49	  starts mixing concerns.
    50	- **No magic numbers or strings.** Any literal value with semantic meaning — pixel
    51	  thresholds, retry counts, country codes, feature flag names, status strings, error
    52	  codes — must be a named constant (`const MAX_RETRIES = 3`) or live in a config/enum
    53	  module. Excepted: `0`, `1`, `-1` in obvious idiomatic uses, and string literals that _are_
    54	  the value (e.g. CSS class names, JSX text).
    55	- **Payment credentials — never logged, never persisted client-side.** Gift card numbers,
    56	  gift card PINs, credit card PANs, CVVs and similar secrets must not appear in any
    57	  `console.*` call, Sentry breadcrumb / event, GTM dataLayer push, analytics event, MRT
    58	  access log, or response body returned to the browser beyond a masked form. Never store
    59	  them in `localStorage`, `sessionStorage`, IndexedDB, or cookies — form state lives in
    60	  React only and is cleared on unmount. Submit them in the POST **body**, never as a
    61	  query string (URLs end up in MRT access logs, browser history, Referer headers). After
    62	  submit, render only the serial portion (e.g. `••••••••1234`). Do not add body-logging
    63	  middleware on routes that carry these fields. Logger and Sentry `beforeSend` must
    64	  redact them. See [.docs/prd/giftcards.md §10](../../.docs/prd/giftcards.md) for the
    65	  GiveX-specific rationale (only the card's serial portion may be displayed or logged).
    66	- **`dangerouslySetInnerHTML` must always wrap its value in a sanitizer call**
    67	  (e.g. `DOMPurify.sanitize(...)`) — never pass raw/unsanitized HTML (CMS content,
    68	  API responses, user input). Unsanitized HTML injection is an XSS vector. Enforced
    69	  by a `semgrep.yml` rule at PR review time — get it right at authoring time instead
    70	  of finding out post-review.
    71	
    72	---
    73	
    74	## File naming and folder structure
    75	
    76	- **Zimmermann-authored files and folders:** `camelCase` (e.g. `productTile.tsx`,
    77	  `useWishlist.ts`, `formatPrice.ts`).
    78	- **Override files (mirroring a base Salesforce file):** keep the original kebab-case
    79	  filename and folder name exactly (e.g. `product-tile.tsx`). This makes the origin of a
    80	  file obvious at a glance.
    81	- **Component folder layout:** each component lives in its own folder under
    82	  [overrides/app/components/](../../overrides/app/components/). Use `index.tsx` for the
    83	  component itself so imports stay clean:
    84	
    85	  ```
    86	  overrides/app/components/productTile/
    87	    index.tsx              ← the component
    88	    index.stories.tsx      ← Storybook story
    89	    index.test.ts          ← Vitest (only if logic-heavy)
    90	    types.ts               ← only if props/types are shared with sibling files
    91	    productTile.scss       ← only if Chakra props are insufficient
    92	  ```
    93	
    94	  Import as `import ProductTile from '.../components/productTile'`.
    95	
    96	---
    97	
    98	## Utilities
    99	
   100	- **Pure functions** — no side effects unless clearly intentional and called out in a comment.
   101	- **No imports from `overrides/app/hooks/`** — utilities must not depend on hooks
   102	  (it's the other direction).
   103	- **Vitest required** when the utility has ≥1 conditional branch or performs ≥1
   104	  transformation (currency, locale, mapping, parsing, etc.). Trivial re-exports or
   105	  one-liners don't need a test.
   106	
   107	---
   108	
   109	## Imports
   110	
   111	- **No circular imports** — if file A imports from file B, B must not import from A
   112	  (check one level deep).
   113	- **No `../../../..` chains longer than 3 levels** — flag for path-alias review.
   114	- **No imports from internal `node_modules/@salesforce/...` source paths** — use the
   115	  package's published entrypoints (`@salesforce/retail-react-app/...`).
   116	- **No imports from a later-sprint feature** — cross-check
   117	  `.docs/memory/sprintScope.md`.

    44	- **Australian spelling** in Zimmermann-authored identifiers and copy (`colour`, `centre`,
    45	  `organisation`). Override files keep upstream Salesforce spelling verbatim.
    46	- **Apply DRY, KISS, and SOLID.** Don't repeat logic — extract to a shared utility or hook
    47	  once the same pattern appears in two places. Prefer the simplest design that works; resist
    48	  speculative abstractions. Keep modules to a single responsibility; split a file when it
    49	  starts mixing concerns.
    50	- **No magic numbers or strings.** Any literal value with semantic meaning — pixel
    51	  thresholds, retry counts, country codes, feature flag names, status strings, error
    52	  codes — must be a named constant (`const MAX_RETRIES = 3`) or live in a config/enum
    53	  module. Excepted: `0`, `1`, `-1` in obvious idiomatic uses, and string literals that _are_
    54	  the value (e.g. CSS class names, JSX text).
    55	- **Payment credentials — never logged, never persisted client-side.** Gift card numbers,
    56	  gift card PINs, credit card PANs, CVVs and similar secrets must not appear in any
    57	  `console.*` call, Sentry breadcrumb / event, GTM dataLayer push, analytics event, MRT
    58	  access log, or response body returned to the browser beyond a masked form. Never store
    59	  them in `localStorage`, `sessionStorage`, IndexedDB, or cookies — form state lives in
    60	  React only and is cleared on unmount. Submit them in the POST **body**, never as a
    61	  query string (URLs end up in MRT access logs, browser history, Referer headers). After
    62	  submit, render only the serial portion (e.g. `••••••••1234`). Do not add body-logging
    63	  middleware on routes that carry these fields. Logger and Sentry `beforeSend` must
    64	  redact them. See [.docs/prd/giftcards.md §10](../../.docs/prd/giftcards.md) for the
    65	  GiveX-specific rationale (only the card's serial portion may be displayed or logged).
    66	- **`dangerouslySetInnerHTML` must always wrap its value in a sanitizer call**
    67	  (e.g. `DOMPurify.sanitize(...)`) — never pass raw/unsanitized HTML (CMS content,
    68	  API responses, user input). Unsanitized HTML injection is an XSS vector. Enforced
    69	  by a `semgrep.yml` rule at PR review time — get it right at authoring time instead
    70	  of finding out post-review.
    71	
    72	---
    73	
    74	## File naming and folder structure
    75	
    76	- **Zimmermann-authored files and folders:** `camelCase` (e.g. `productTile.tsx`,
    77	  `useWishlist.ts`, `formatPrice.ts`).
    78	- **Override files (mirroring a base Salesforce file):** keep the original kebab-case
    79	  filename and folder name exactly (e.g. `product-tile.tsx`). This makes the origin of a
    80	  file obvious at a glance.
    81	- **Component folder layout:** each component lives in its own folder under
    82	  [overrides/app/components/](../../overrides/app/components/). Use `index.tsx` for the
    83	  component itself so imports stay clean:
    84	
    85	  ```
    86	  overrides/app/components/productTile/
    87	    index.tsx              ← the component
    88	    index.stories.tsx      ← Storybook story
    89	    index.test.ts          ← Vitest (only if logic-heavy)
    90	    types.ts               ← only if props/types are shared with sibling files
    91	    productTile.scss       ← only if Chakra props are insufficient
    92	  ```
    93	
    94	  Import as `import ProductTile from '.../components/productTile'`.
    95	
    96	---
    97	
    98	## Utilities
    99	
   100	- **Pure functions** — no side effects unless clearly intentional and called out in a comment.
   101	- **No imports from `overrides/app/hooks/`** — utilities must not depend on hooks
   102	  (it's the other direction).
   103	- **Vitest required** when the utility has ≥1 conditional branch or performs ≥1
   104	  transformation (currency, locale, mapping, parsing, etc.). Trivial re-exports or
   105	  one-liners don't need a test.
   106	
   107	---
   108	
   109	## Imports
   110	
   111	- **No circular imports** — if file A imports from file B, B must not import from A
   112	  (check one level deep).
   113	- **No `../../../..` chains longer than 3 levels** — flag for path-alias review.
   114	- **No imports from internal `node_modules/@salesforce/...` source paths** — use the
   115	  package's published entrypoints (`@salesforce/retail-react-app/...`).
   116	- **No imports from a later-sprint feature** — cross-check
   117	  `.docs/memory/sprintScope.md`.

=== css.md ===
     1	# CSS & Styling Conventions
     2	
     3	Chakra UI and `.scss` conventions. See [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md) > Rules > Styling for the
     4	higher-level policy (Chakra props first, `.scss` only when insufficient, theme file
     5	ownership/tiers) — this file covers the concrete day-to-day rules underneath that policy.
     6	
     7	---
     8	
     9	## Tokens — no hardcoded design values
    10	
    11	Chakra UI props must use the Chakra token system — no hardcoded hex colours, no pixel
    12	values for spacing, no raw font sizes. Tokens belong in
    13	[overrides/app/theme/foundation/](../../overrides/app/theme/) (Tier 1 — see
    14	[frozenFiles.md](./frozenFiles.md)).
    15	
    16	```tsx
    17	// ❌ hardcoded
    18	<Box color="#1A1A1A" padding="16px" fontSize="14px" />
    19	
    20	// ✅ token
    21	<Box color="brand.primary" padding={4} fontSize="sm" />
    22	```
    23	
    24	**Not currently mechanically enforced.** Unlike the accessibility rules in
    25	[components.md](./components.md), there's no `.coderabbit/ast-grep-rules/` rule watching for
    26	a raw hex code or `px` value landing in a Chakra prop or `.scss` file yet — this is a strong
    27	candidate for the same treatment (ast-grep can pattern-match a hex-colour or `px` literal
    28	inside a JSX attribute value) if hardcoded values keep slipping through review.
    29	
    30	---
    31	
    32	## `.scss` — only when Chakra props are insufficient
    33	
    34	Per AGENTS.md, reach for a `.scss` file alongside a component only when Chakra's prop system
    35	genuinely can't express what's needed (e.g. complex pseudo-selectors, keyframe animations,
    36	print styles). When you do:
    37	
    38	- **File naming:** matches the component file exactly — `productTile.scss` next to
    39	  `productTile/index.tsx` (see [conventions.md](./conventions.md) > File naming and folder
    40	  structure for the folder layout this sits in).
    41	- **Scoped, co-located only.** No global stylesheets outside `overrides/app/theme/` — a
    42	  component's `.scss` file must only affect that component's own markup.
    43	- **Nesting depth ≤ 3 levels.** Beyond that, the selector is almost always reaching into a
    44	  child component's internals rather than styling its own root — a sign the styling belongs
    45	  in that child instead, or that Chakra's `sx` prop / a theme variant would express it more
    46	  directly.
    47	- **No ID selectors.** Class-based only — an ID selector's specificity makes it
    48	  disproportionately hard to override later (including by a legitimate future Chakra
    49	  variant), and IDs aren't guaranteed unique when a component renders more than once on a
    50	  page.
    51	- **No `!important`** without an inline comment explaining why the override is genuinely
    52	  unavoidable (e.g. fighting a third-party widget's inline styles) — same reasoning as the
    53	  `any`/non-null-assertion escape hatches in [typescript.md](./typescript.md): allowed, but
    54	  the reason has to be visible at the point of use, not left for the next reader to guess.
    55	- **Prefer Chakra's `sx` prop or a theme variant extension over a new `.scss` file** for
    56	  anything that's really just "a Chakra style the prop system doesn't have a named prop for"
    57	  — a new global class is a bigger footprint than a one-off `sx` override, and `sx` keeps the
    58	  style co-located with the JSX that uses it instead of a separate file to keep in sync.

503	                        after "CONNECT WITH US" ends at y=72, so only its own 4px padding-top

509	                      </chakra.li>

512	                </chakra.div>
513	              ))}
514	            </chakra.div>
515	          </chakra.div>

521	              buildUrl + history.push rather than useNavigation. styles.logoButton is a chrome
522	              reset only, so the logo keeps its own geometry. */}

524	            <ZimmLogo variant="inverse" />
525	          </chakra.button>

527	      </chakra.div>

=== overrideStyling.md ===
     1	# Styling an Override Component
     2	
     3	How to style a component under `overrides/app/components/` or `overrides/app/theme/`.
     4	Cross-references [overrides.md](./overrides.md) (module-replacement correctness — a
     5	different concern: that file is about not breaking SFCC's own imports, this one is
     6	about what values to reach for once the component compiles). Day-to-day CSS/token
     7	rules live in [css.md](./css.md); this file is the practical "what do I actually type"
     8	companion.
     9	
    10	---
    11	
    12	## The hierarchy — reach for these in order
    13	
    14	1. **`textStyle` prop** for anything textual. `textStyle="body2"`, never a raw `fontSize`.
    15	   All 22 Handover text styles are registered in `theme/foundation/typography.ts`.
    16	2. **Semantic colour/spacing token strings** — `color="text.default"`, `bg="background.02"`,
    17	   `spacing="m"`, `padding={{ base: 'm', md: 'xl' }}`. These resolve through
    18	   `theme.colors`/`theme.space` (both registered — see `theme/index.ts`'s own comment
    19	   for which foundation scales are and aren't registered, and why).
    20	3. **A component's own theme config** (`theme/components/<name>.ts`) for anything that
    21	   needs to vary by variant/size/state and isn't already a Chakra prop — see
    22	   "Component-local tokens" below. For an interactive component with existing Chakra
    23	   support (buttons, inputs, etc.), this theme config is the single source of truth —
    24	   see "One canonical styling surface per component type" below.
    25	4. **`sx` prop** for a one-off Chakra-prop-system gap, per [css.md](./css.md).
    26	5. **Scoped `.scss`** only when `sx` genuinely can't express it (complex pseudo-selectors,
    27	   keyframes) — same file, same rules as [css.md](./css.md) already documents.
    28	
    29	**Never**: a raw hex/px/rem/em literal in a component file — reach for the token
    30	instead. The one standing exception is `button.ts`'s provisional height/padding
    31	constants (`BTN_HEIGHT_LG`/`BTN_HEIGHT_SM`/`BTN_PADDING_Y`), pending UI-designer
    32	sign-off — see Units below. Run `node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs` before opening
    33	a PR that touches `overrides/app/components/**` or `overrides/app/theme/components/**`
    34	— it greps for exactly this. It is not wired into CI yet — that's a reasonable next
    35	step once someone owns triaging its false positives (hairline px is expected and
    36	not a bug; see below).
    37	
    38	## Units
    39	
    40	- **`rem`** for anything that should scale with the user's root font-size / browser zoom
    41	  (WCAG 1.4.4): type (`fontSize`, `lineHeight`, `letterSpacing`) and spacing
    42	  (`spacing.ts`'s named scale). Letter-spacing values that were specified as sub-pixel px
    43	  in the source don't round to clean rem numbers, so those keep a trailing `// -0.12px`
    44	  comment for traceability.
    45	- **`px`** for hairline geometry that should _not_ scale: border widths, focus-ring
    46	  offsets, and (for now) the provisional button-height constants in `button.ts` that are
    47	  still pending UI-designer sign-off against Handover.
    48	- **`em`** only for breakpoints (`gridSystem.ts` — deliberate, so `.zimm-grid`'s media
    49	  queries shift with zoom the same way Chakra's responsive props do) and other
    50	  genuinely context-relative cases. Not a general-purpose unit.
    51	
    52	## The alias tier is a reference, not a second copy
    53	
    54	`theme/foundation/colour.ts`'s primitive tier (`grey`, `ivory`, ...) is defined first as
    55	plain `const`s, and the semantic/alias tier below it (`text`, `background`, `border`,
    56	...) reads from those consts (`text.default: grey[900]`) instead of retyping the hex
    57	value. Do the same for any new primitive/alias pair you add — two values can't disagree
    58	if only one of them is ever typed.
    59	
    60	`zimmTokens.ts` (the `--zimm-*` CSS-var registry for `globalStyles.ts`'s `.zimm-*`
    61	classes) is fully derived the same way — it imports `colors`/`spacing`/`fontSizes`/
    62	`lineHeights`/`letterSpacings`/`fontWeights`/`iconSizes`/`actionSizes`/`motion`/`grid`
    63	from their owning files rather than retyping values. The only literals left are the 7
    64	numeric `--zimm-scale-NNN` aliases with no named-scale equivalent (`025`, `700`, `1100`,
    65	`1200`, `1300`, `3500`, `4500`) — not duplicates, just Handover values with nothing to
    66	derive them from. `theme/index.test.tsx`'s collision-guard tests still exist as a
    67	regression net; treat a failure there as a real drift signal, not test noise.
    68	
    69	## One canonical styling surface per component type
    70	
    71	Only one place should define how a given interactive component looks: its
    72	`theme/components/<name>.ts` config, consumed via Chakra's component (`<Button>`,
    73	`<Link>` variant, etc.). Don't also give it a `.zimm-*` global class in
    74	`globalStyles.ts` — a static CSS class can't express `_hover`/`_active`/`_disabled`/
    75	`_focusVisible` states the way a Chakra theme config can, so a class "mirror" is
    76	structurally incomplete from the start, and nothing stops its values from disagreeing
    77	with the real theme config over time. `button.ts` is the single source of truth for
    78	button styling; `globalStyles.ts` has no `.zimm-btn-*` classes — use Chakra's `<Button>`
    79	for any button, not a class.
    80	
    81	`.zimm-*` classes remain the right tool for genuinely static, non-interactive,
    82	massively-reused treatments (typography, the responsive grid, form-field layout) where
    83	there's no interactive state to lose.
    84	
    85	## Importing an already-overridden component from a new component
    86	
    87	If component A (e.g. `productDetailOptions`) uses component B, and B already has an
    88	override (e.g. `swatch-group`), **import B via a relative path
    89	(`'../swatch-group'`), not the SFCC base path
    90	(`'@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/swatch-group'`)** — even though the
    91	base path is exactly what [overrides.md](./overrides.md) requires _inside_ an override
    92	that's itself shadowing an SFCC module (see `product-tile/index.tsx`'s `DisplayPrice`
    93	import, which is correct for that file).
    94	
    95	The reason the two cases differ: the resolver that redirects
    96	`@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` imports to `overrides/` (`ccExtensibility` in
    97	`package.json`, read by a webpack plugin) only runs in the **real app build** — dev
    98	server and production. `.storybook/main.js` aliases that package straight to
    99	`node_modules` and `vitest.config.ts` doesn't touch it at all, so neither loads the
   100	resolver. A base-path import of an already-overridden component will build and run
   101	correctly in the shipped app, but silently render/test the **unstyled base SFCC
   102	version** in Storybook and Vitest — the story or test looks like it's exercising your
   103	override and isn't.
   104	
   105	**Known instance of this, not yet fixed:** `product-tile/index.tsx`'s `DisplayPrice`
   106	import uses the base path. Currently dormant only because its Storybook story exercises
   107	the `CardBaseline` named export (which takes `price` as a pre-rendered node and never
   108	calls `DisplayPrice`), not the default `ProductTile` bridge that actually renders it —
   109	worth fixing before anything writes a story/test against the default export.
   110	
   111	An override component's own base-path imports (of modules it is _not_ also
   112	overriding) are unaffected by this — `RecommendedProducts`, `Seo`, `QuantityPicker`
   113	etc. have no local override to miss, so the base path is simply correct for them.
   114	
   115	## Component-local tokens
   116	
   117	When a component needs a spacing/sizing value that already has a `spacing.ts` /
   118	`iconSizes` / etc. entry, reference it **by name** in the theme config
   119	(`marginBottom: 'xs'`, not `marginBottom: 2` or `marginBottom: '0.5rem'`) — Chakra
   120	resolves named scale keys against the registered `theme.space` automatically. See
   121	`theme/components/imageGallery.ts` / `swatchGroup.ts` for the pattern: both re-express

    14	1. **`textStyle` prop** for anything textual. `textStyle="body2"`, never a raw `fontSize`.

     3	import { ChakraProvider } from '@chakra-ui/react';

     5	import theme from '../overrides/app/theme';
     6	import { ZimmTokensGlobal } from '../overrides/app/theme/zimmTokensGlobal';

     8	
     9	// ZimmTokensGlobal injects the --zimm-* :root custom properties, mirroring what
    10	// _app-config does in the app. Without it, the .zimm-* global classes and the
    11	// var(--zimm-*) component overrides (button/header/listMenu) render unresolved in
    12	// Storybook. Same shared source as the app, so the two cannot drift.
    13	//
    14	// ZimmFontFace declares the self-hosted Futura Round faces, likewise mirroring
    15	// _app-config. Without it Storybook renders the fallback stack while the app renders
    16	// Futura Round — the fallback measures ~13% wider, so any visual comparison made in
    17	// Storybook would not match the app or Figma. Font files are served here by the
    18	// staticDirs mapping in .storybook/main.js.

    22	    <ZimmTokensGlobal />
    23	    <Story />
    24	  </ChakraProvider>

    34	  parameters: {
    35	    controls: {
    36	      matchers: {

    39	      },

    46	      // without an accessible name — a known upstream limitation. Exclude them
    47	      // from all a11y checks since they are framework-level, not component output.
    48	      context: {

=== testing.md (first 120) ===
1	# Testing Conventions
2	
3	Three layers, three purposes. **Do not duplicate coverage across layers** — pick the cheapest layer that proves the behaviour.
4	
5	| Layer | Tool | What it covers | File pattern | CI gate |
6	|---|---|---|---|---|
7	| Unit | Vitest | Pure logic, data mapping, transforms, hook behaviour in isolation | `*.test.ts` co-located with the source | Every PR (`qa.yml`) |
8	| Component interaction | Storybook `play` | User-facing interactions in a single component (clicks, form fills, focus management) | `*.stories.tsx` `play` function | Every PR (`qa.yml`) |
9	| E2E | Playwright | Full user journeys across pages, multi-region, integration boundaries | `e2e/tests/**/*.spec.{ts,js}` | Every PR (`qa.yml`) — desktop + mobile Chromium against localhost/dev API; BrowserStack multi-browser on `release/**` only |
10	
11	> Higher-level project rules: [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md) > Testing. Day-to-day file conventions: [conventions.md](./conventions.md). This file describes **how** to write tests at each layer.
12	
13	---
14	
15	## What to test (and what to skip)
16	
17	Write tests where failure would be **non-obvious** or **costly to debug**:
18	
19	- ✅ Data mapping: Contentful → component props, locale/currency transforms, SFCC payload → view model
20	- ✅ Integration boundaries: Global-e pricing/tax logic, checkout ownership branching, consent gating
21	- ✅ Complex state: cart mutations, consent state changes, multi-step flows, optimistic-update rollback
22	- ✅ Pure logic that would survive a refactor invisibly if broken
23	- ❌ Re-exports, one-line passthroughs, type-only helpers
24	- ❌ Storybook visual snapshots — Chromatic/Loki belongs in a separate budget, not Vitest
25	- ❌ The framework — don't test that React renders, that Chakra applies styles, or that React Query caches
26	
27	---
28	
29	## Layer 1 — Vitest (unit)
30	
31	### File layout
32	
33	Co-located with the source, `.test.ts` suffix, never `.spec.ts`:
34	
35	```
36	overrides/app/utils/formatPrice.ts
37	overrides/app/utils/formatPrice.test.ts
38	overrides/app/hooks/useCurrency.ts
39	overrides/app/hooks/useCurrency.test.ts
40	```
41	
42	Components use `index.test.ts` next to `index.tsx` in the component folder
43	(see [components.md](./components.md) > Components).
44	
45	### Structure
46	
47	- `describe` blocks group related cases; `test` (or `it`) for individual cases.
48	- **Arrange → Act → Assert** pattern, one behaviour per test.
49	- Test names describe the behaviour, not the implementation: `"converts AUD to USD using the latest Global-e rate"` not `"calls convertCurrency"`.
50	- Use `beforeEach` for setup; clear mocks with `vi.clearAllMocks()` after each test.
51	
52	### Mocking
53	
54	- **Inline mock objects** for isolated unit tests — define plain JS objects right in the test file.
55	- **`vi.mock()`** for module-level stubs. Mock the smallest possible surface: a single function, not a whole module, when feasible.
56	- **MSW** is allowed for cross-functional integration tests (multiple modules wired together). Production paths must never depend on MSW — see AGENTS.md > Rules > "No mocking."
57	- Do not mock the thing under test; do not assert on internal implementation calls when an output assertion would do.
58	
59	### Commerce SDK hooks
60	
61	Hooks that call `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` (e.g. `useCurrentBasket`, `useCurrentCustomer`) need a `QueryClientProvider` and `CommerceApiProvider` wrapper. Build a small `renderWithProviders` helper in `overrides/app/test-utils/` rather than duplicating wrapper boilerplate per test.
62	
63	### What NOT to write at this layer
64	
65	- Visual rendering — that's Storybook
66	- Cross-page navigation — that's Playwright
67	- Real network calls — never; use MSW or stubbed hooks
68	
69	---
70	
71	## Layer 2 — Storybook `play` (component interaction)
72	
73	### When to use `play`
74	
75	Every UI component has a `*.stories.tsx` (see [components.md](./components.md) > Storybook). Add a `play` function when there is **interactive behaviour worth asserting**:
76	
77	- Form validation triggers on blur / submit
78	- Disclosure (accordion, drawer, modal) opens / closes via keyboard + mouse
79	- Focus moves correctly through a flow
80	- A controlled input's onChange wires through to the rendered output
81	
82	If the story is purely visual (renders different prop combinations), no `play` is needed.
83	
84	### Pattern
85	
86	```tsx
87	import {expect, userEvent, within} from '@storybook/test'
88	
89	export const SubmitDisabledUntilValid: Story = {
90	    play: async ({canvasElement}) => {
91	        const canvas = within(canvasElement)
92	        const submit = canvas.getByRole('button', {name: /submit/i})
93	        await expect(submit).toBeDisabled()
94	        await userEvent.type(canvas.getByLabelText(/email/i), 'name@example.com')
95	        await expect(submit).toBeEnabled()
96	    }
97	}
98	```
99	
100	- Always query through `within(canvasElement)` — never reach into `document` directly.
101	- Use **`getByRole`** with an accessible name as the first-choice selector. Fall back to `getByLabelText` for form fields, `getByText` last.
102	- Don't import `userEvent` from `@testing-library/user-event` — use the Storybook re-export so the action is logged in the timeline.
103	
104	### What NOT to write at this layer
105	
106	- Multi-page flows — that's Playwright
107	- Heavy API mocking — keep stories visual, push integration assertions to Playwright
108	
109	---
110	
111	## Layer 3 — Playwright (E2E)
112	
113	### Workflow
114	
115	E2E tests follow the **three-stage gherkin-first workflow** (see [.claude/skills/qa-generate/](../skills/qa-generate/SKILL.md)):
116	
117	1. Claude (or any developer) drafts a `.feature` file with Gherkin scenarios
118	2. Lead QA validates in plain English — **no Playwright code is written until sign-off**
119	3. Playwright spec is generated only after the `.feature` is approved
120

=== components/button/index.tsx (export style contrast) ===
     1	import React from 'react';
     2	import { Button as ChakraButton, chakra, type ButtonProps as ChakraButtonProps } from '@chakra-ui/react';
     3	
     4	export type ButtonProps = Omit<ChakraButtonProps, 'variant' | 'size'> & {
     5	  variant?: 'primary' | 'secondary';
     6	  size?: 'lg' | 'sm';
     7	  /**
     8	   * Optional price label displayed on the right-hand side of a large button
     9	   * (e.g. "Add to Bag" + "$575"). Only renders when `size` is `'lg'`.
    10	   */
    11	  price?: string;
    12	};
    13	
    14	/**
    15	 * Zimmermann branded button. Two variants (primary/secondary) and two sizes
    16	 * (lg/sm) — all states (hover, pressed, disabled, focused) are handled via the
    17	 * Chakra theme in `overrides/app/theme/components/button.ts`.
    18	 *
    19	 * Pass `price` to show a split-label large button (e.g. "ADD TO BAG $575").
    20	 * The button defaults to `w="full"` in that case so justify-between has room
    21	 * to spread; override via the `w` prop if a fixed width is needed.
    22	 */
    23	export const Button = ({ children, variant = 'primary', size = 'lg', price, ...rest }: ButtonProps) => {
    24	  if (price && size === 'lg') {
    25	    return (
    26	      <ChakraButton variant={variant} size={size} w="full" justifyContent="space-between" gap={4} {...rest}>
    27	        <chakra.span>{children}</chakra.span>
    28	        <chakra.span>{price}</chakra.span>
    29	      </ChakraButton>
    30	    );
    31	  }
    32	
    33	  return (
    34	    <ChakraButton variant={variant} size={size} {...rest}>
    35	      {children}
    36	    </ChakraButton>
    37	  );
    38	};

File layout per component (VERIFIED — `git ls-tree -r --name-only`) The entire `ui-kits` tree on that branch is **12 files, two per component, no exceptions**: ``` overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmButton/{index.tsx, index.stories.tsx} overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmIcon/{index.tsx, index.stories.tsx} overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmLogo/{index.tsx, index.stories.tsx} overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmNavItem/{index.tsx, index.stories.tsx} overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmTextInput/{index.tsx, index.stories.tsx} overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmInputAction/{index.tsx, index.stories.tsx} ``` No `types.ts`, no `.scss`, no `README`, no sub-components, **no `index.test.ts` anywhere**. **Co-located tests: zero.** `git ls-tree -r --name-only -- overrides/app/components/ | grep -E "test|spec"` returns nothing — there is not a single test file under `overrides/app/components/` on that branch. All 10 test files are: ``` overrides/app/hooks/{useContentfulClient,useCountryConfig,useSubscribeModal,useZimmTextInputState}.test.* overrides/app/theme/components/{recipeGuards,zimmTextInput}.test.ts overrides/app/theme/{fontFace.test.tsx,index.test.tsx} overrides/app/utils/safeHref.test.ts e2e/tests/zimm/homepage/SMOKE-homepage-load.spec.js ``` **That is the load-bearing pattern:** testable logic is *moved out of the component* and unit-tested where it lands — the value/focus state → `overrides/app/hooks/useZimmTextInputState.ts` (+ `.test.ts`), the colour cascade → `theme/components/zimmTextInput.ts` exported resolvers (+ `.test.ts`), the href allowlist → `overrides/app/utils/safeHref.ts` (+ `.test.ts`). The component file itself is covered only by Storybook `play`. ## Which atoms have a recipe | Atom | Recipe | What it uses instead | |---|---|---| | `zimmNavItem` | **Yes** — `theme/components/zimmNavItem.ts` (single-part) | — | | `zimmTextInput` | **Yes** — `theme/components/zimmTextInput.ts` (multipart) | — | | `zimmButton` | **No** | Reuses the existing `theme/components/button.ts` (`Button` recipe): maps its props onto Chakra `variant`/`size` names (`primary`/`secondary`/`icon` + `*Inverse`; sizes `lg`/`sm`/`icon`) | | `zimmIcon` | **No** | Direct props: `boxSize={iconSizes[size]}` with `iconSizes` imported from `app/theme/foundation` | | `zimmLogo` | **No** | Raw inline `style={{...}}` on the `

` (`:127`). **`.../molecules/zimmInputAction/index.tsx`** (82 lines) - Named consts `DEFAULT_INPUT_NAME` / `VALIDATION_EMPTY` / `VALIDATION_EMAIL` (`:20-22`). - Composes the two atoms; the button goes through `ZimmTextInput`'s `trailing` slot (`:69-78`). - Caller error wins: `errorText={errorText ?? validationError}` (`:67`). --- # 3. Recipe anatomy ## `overrides/app/theme/components/zimmNavItem.ts` (78 lines) — single-part ```ts import { defineStyleConfig } from '@chakra-ui/react'; // :1 export const ZimmNavItem = defineStyleConfig({ // :74 baseStyle, variants, defaultProps: { variant: 'light' }, }); ``` - **No `parts`, no `sizes`.** `baseStyle` is a plain object (`:13-53`), not a function. - `variants` (`:55-72`) = `light` and `inverse`, each carrying **only** `color` + `_focusVisible`. - States are nested selectors, not extra parts: `'& > span'` (`:42-45`, the underline carrier), `_hover` (`:46-48`), `'&[aria-current="page"] > span'` (`:50-52`). Value forms and which props they are used on: - **Bare `textStyle` key** — `textStyle: 'navigation'` (`:17`). This is the canonical way type is set. - **`var(--zimm-*)`** — `fontFamily` (`:18`), `minHeight` (`:23`), `lineHeight` (`:28`), the border-width inside the `borderBottom` shorthand (`:43`), duration+easing inside `transition` (`:44`), `color` in both variants (`:57`, `:65`), `outline` + `outlineOffset` (`:59-60`, `:67-68`). - **Raw literal, hoisted to a named const** — `const NAV_ITEM_PAD_Y = '4.5px';` (`:11`) used on `paddingBlock` (`:29`), with an 8-line derivation (`:3-10`) ending "No 4.5px entry exists in spacing.ts — same provisional treatment as button.ts's BTN_PADDING_Y, pending UI-designer sign-off." - **Bare CSS keywords** for non-token properties: `display: 'inline-flex'`, `whiteSpace: 'normal'`, `cursor: 'pointer'`, `background: 'none'`, `border: 'none'`, `paddingInline: 0`, `textDecoration: 'none'`. - **Zero bare spacing/sizing token keys.** `minHeight` deliberately uses `var(--zimm-scale-xl)` and not `'xl'` — that is recipeGuards invariant #1. - Two comments worth copying verbatim as a style: `:36-38` explains `paddingInline` instead of the `padding` shorthand (a shorthand after `paddingBlock` would reset it); `:24-27` explains why `minHeight` + line-height, not centring. ## `overrides/app/theme/components/zimmTextInput.ts` (186 lines) — multipart, hand-rolled ```ts import type { SystemStyleObject } from '@chakra-ui/react'; // :1 (type-only import) export const ZimmTextInput = { // :76 parts: ['root','row','content','label','input','clearButton','helper','error'], // :77 baseStyle: (props: ZimmTextInputStyleProps): Record => { ... }, // :78 }; ``` - **Not** `defineMultiStyleConfig`, **not** `createMultiStyleConfigHelpers`, **no** `anatomy`. Plain object literal. `git grep -nE "defineStyleConfig|defineMultiStyleConfig|createMultiStyleConfigHelpers|anatomy"` over `overrides/app/theme` returns exactly 4 hits: `button.ts:1,243` and `zimmNavItem.ts:1,74`. `footer.ts` (`ZimmFooter`, `:47`) is the same hand-rolled `{ parts, baseStyle }` shape. - **No `variants`, no `sizes`, no `defaultProps`.** Every state is a recipe *prop* consumed by the `baseStyle` function. - `export type ZimmTextInputStyleProps` (`:42-49`) is the contract the component passes in. - Three **exported pure resolvers** — `resolveBorderColour` (`:54`), `resolveHoverBorderColour` (`:64`), `resolveLabelColour` (`:69`) — exported specifically so `zimmTextInput.test.ts` can assert the cascade. Value forms and which props they are used on: - **`var(--zimm-*)`** — every colour, every font family/size/weight/lineHeight, the border width, and both sizing values. The two sizing ones each carry an explicit justification: `:126` `height: 'var(--zimm-scale-l)', // 20px — var, not 'l': theme.sizes has no 'l' key` and `:151-153` `// var, not 'xl': min-width/height resolve via theme.sizes (xl = 36rem), not theme.space`. - **Bare spacing token keys, only on space-resolving props** — `gap: 'xs'` (`:94`), `paddingTop`/`paddingBottom: '2xs'` (`:96-97`), `top: '3xs'` (`:114`), `marginTop: '2xs'` (`:165`, `:174`). - **Named consts for literals with no token** — `LABEL_FLOATED_SIZE`/`LABEL_FLOATED_WEIGHT` (`:24-25`, both `var()`), `FIELD_CONTENT_HEIGHT = '2.25rem'` (`:35`, preceded by an 8-line rem-not-px WCAG 1.4.4 rationale citing `overrideStyling.md > Units` and the footer's `SIZE_SUBSCRIBE_SLOT` derivation), `OPACITY_DISABLED = 0.4` (`:37`, "No opacity token in foundation yet — pending Tier 1 PR"), `MOTION` (`:39`). - **JS-computed conditionals** — `const floated = Boolean(focused || filled)` then `fontWeight: floated ? … : …` (`:110`), `top: floated ? '3xs' : '50%'` (`:114`), `_hover: disabled ? undefined : {...}` (`:100`). ## Naming convention and registration (VERIFIED) - **Registered theme key = the exact PascalCase component name.** `ZimmNavItem`, `ZimmTextInput`, `ZimmFooter`. The exported const name in the recipe file === the theme key === the string passed to `useStyleConfig`/`useMultiStyleConfig`. - **Recipe filename = camelCase, matching the component folder name**: `theme/components/zimmNavItem.ts` ↔ `ui-kits/atoms/zimmNavItem/`. - The `Zimm` prefix is mandatory for anything that would otherwise collide with an SFCC base recipe — `footer.ts` exports `ZimmFooter`, not `Footer`, and `recipeGuards.test.ts:212-228` enforces it. - Registration in `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` (15 lines total) is a two-line edit: ```ts import { ZimmNavItem } from './zimmNavItem'; // :5 export const components = { Button, ZimmFooter, Header, ListMenu, ZimmNavItem, ZimmTextInput }; // :8-15 ``` Plain object literal, no `satisfies`, keys not alphabetised. `theme/index.ts:58` spreads `components` into `extendTheme(baseTheme, overrides)` (`:51-64`). - Consumption: `useStyleConfig('ZimmNavItem', { variant })` (`zimmNavItem/index.tsx:33`), `useMultiStyleConfig('ZimmTextInput', {...})` (`zimmTextInput/index.tsx:80`) — inline string literals. Contrast `footer/index.tsx:28` `const ZIMM_FOOTER_RECIPE = 'ZimmFooter';` used at 5 call sites. See §8(j). --- # 4. `overrides/app/theme/components/navConstants.ts` — the whole file is 5 lines ```ts // Shared prototype nav letter-spacing value — used by header.ts's desktopActionButton // and listMenu.ts's listMenuTriggerLink. The design system's .zimm-text-nav / // textStyles.navigation both specify 0px — unresolved with the UI designer, so this // prototype value is kept rather than silently switched. See PR description. export const NAV_LETTER_SPACING = '0.02em'; ``` What it holds: exactly one value. Why it is separate from a recipe: 1. It is **shared by two different recipes** (`header.ts` and `listMenu.ts`). Putting it in either would make one recipe import the other — banned by `conventions.md:110-111` (no circular imports) and structurally wrong. 2. It is **not a style config** — it can't be registered in `components/index.ts`, so it needs a non-recipe home inside `theme/components/`. 3. It doubles as a **documented disagreement record**: the value contradicts the design system's own `0px`, and the comment says so rather than silently reconciling. It takes letter-spacing from `textStyle: 'navigation'` → `letterSpacings.sm`. `navConstants` is header/listMenu-only. --- # 5. `overrides/app/theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts` (230 lines) Not a per-recipe test — **one file that walks the entire registered recipe map**. A 33-line file-header docblock (`:1-33`) explains the shared failure shape: "the value is a *valid* `SystemStyleObject` entry, so TypeScript is satisfied; no lint rule covers it; and nothing asserts layout." Rationale: `width:'xl'` reads `theme.sizes.xl` = 36rem | | `no typography property uses a bare scale key` | `:186` | `TYPOGRAPHY_PROPS` Map (`:78-82`) for `fontSize`/`lineHeight`/`letterSpacing`, each set = own scale keys ∪ spacing keys. `fontWeight` deliberately excluded (`:76-77`: `medium` is a valid key in both scales) | | `no compound shorthand contains a bare scale key` | `:196` | `padding,margin,inset,gap,p,m` (`:85`) — masks `var(...)`→`VAR`, splits on whitespace, flags any bare scale key. `padding: 'xs 0'` is emitted verbatim and dropped by the browser | | `no recipe silently inherits a base SFCC recipe of the same name` | `:212` | `INTENTIONAL_MERGES = ['Button','Header','ListMenu']` (`:216`); every other key must be namespaced. **This is the test a new recipe interacts with** — `ZimmFoo` passes, `Breadcrumb` fails | **Yes, it has a self-test proving it can fail** — `:168-174`: ```ts test('collect() actually walks the registered recipes', () => { // Every other test here asserts an empty offender list, which an empty input satisfies // just as well as a clean one.
